shared_elements: upright freestanding carved stone monument on museum plinth
anthropomorphic figure occupying most of the surface
elaborate headdress/head ornament at top of the composition
circular disc or medallion on the chest region
low-relief incised curvilinear ornament / scroll motifs
banded or belt-like horizontal element across the lower body
justification: Both stones present a single frontally-oriented figure whose ornate headdress fills the upper zone, a prominent circular chest disc at mid-height, and a belt/band across the lower torso, which is a fairly specific shared compositional scheme. The manner of execution differs sharply, however: A is a thick, boulder-like dark stone with deep, rounded, weather-blurred modelling and few discrete motifs, while B is a thin, pale rectangular slab covered edge-to-edge with crisp, shallow, linear relief including small block-like glyph panels.
